title: Test multi-process budget behavior with two trackers on one fake Redis server
answers: how to test gateway budget tracker across multiple processes
simulate two gateway processes sharing redis budget window in tests
fakeredis shared server for budget tracker tests
write regression test for stale budget policy version
body:
To reproduce cross-process behavior, build two RedisBudgetTracker instances on one fakeredis.FakeServer, each with its own fakeredis.FakeRedis(server=server, decode_responses=True) client, via the helper _make_shared_trackers in tests/gateway/test_redis_budget_tracker.py.
Drive one tracker with the stale policy (refresh_policies, record_cost) and assert the other tracker's should_reject_request result, so the test exercises the shared Redis window rather than in-memory state.
Use decode_responses=True so hash values compare as strings, matching how the Lua script's stored duration fields are read back.
The PR also verified Lua-script changes by hand against a real Redis server, since fakeredis may not match Lua behavior exactly; do the same for changes to _ENSURE_WINDOW_LUA.
applies: Tests for RedisBudgetTracker behavior that depends on state shared between processes.
says: The AI gateway exceeds spending limits when multiple worker processes handle incoming requests.
Requests are not rejected after another server worker has already exhausted the budget window.
Budget limits should stay synchronized across parallel gateway instances under heavy traffic.
Outdated budget policies allow requests to pass even when total spending is capped.
